nodes.description: Foregut symptoms in hEDS are predominantly functional. In 114 hEDS/HSD patients with reflux symptoms (229 including patient controls) studied by 24-hour pH-impedance, Rome IV functional heartburn was the commonest diagnosis and pathological reflux was no more frequent than in non-hypermobile patient controls; high-resolution manometry found hEDS not associated with esophageal dysmotility. The gastroenterology society frames the hEDS gut phenotype as disorders of gut-brain interaction. The sensory or central process behind the functional symptoms has not been identified in hEDS, and whether it shares a mechanism with somatic central sensitization is untested.

nodes.description: Candidate molecular lesion from one 2025 study. Whole-exome sequencing of 200 hEDS patients found rare variants across the kallikrein gene family, including a recurrent KLK15 p.Gly226Asp missense variant segregating in two multigenerational families. KLK15 is a secreted serine protease that binds fibronectin and lysyl oxidase (LOX); in a knock-in mouse the variant acted as a dominant negative, displacing KLK15 and LOX from insoluble extracellular matrix compartments, with ultrastructural collagen fibril alteration in tendon, valve abnormality and a changed cytokine profile. Unreplicated; the variant is not a diagnostic marker and explains a minority of cases at most.

nodes.description: Non-length-dependent small fiber neuropathy documented by skin biopsy in hEDS, with intraepidermal nerve fiber loss comparable to idiopathic small fiber neuropathy but greater loss of autonomic (sudomotor, pilomotor and vasomotor) fibers and postganglionic sudomotor failure. Cohorts are selected from autonomic or neuropathy clinics, and an earlier consecutive series found no somatosensory damage by nerve conduction and laser-evoked potentials, so the prevalence in unselected hEDS and the cause of the fiber loss are open. The authors propose it as an intrinsic feature rather than a consequence of joint disease.

nodes.description: Proposed hemodynamic intermediate: lax venous walls distend excessively under ordinary hydrostatic pressure on standing, pooling blood in the splanchnic and lower-limb veins, reducing venous return and preload and provoking compensatory tachycardia. First proposed from a case series of adolescents with chronic fatigue syndrome, orthostatic intolerance and EDS, and described in the 2026 small fiber study as what many authors speculate. A PubMed search in November 2026 for Ehlers-Danlos with venous compliance, distensibility or pooling returned five records and no measurement of venous compliance in hEDS; the only direct measurement is in postural tachycardia of other cause, where compliance was normal, and autonomic testing in hEDS-associated POTS has not differed from POTS of other cause.
